 Figure 1. 2D VLA models (left-top) leverage intuitive semantic perception from multi-view transformers but struggle with explicit 3D                                     Source




 spatial reasoning. 3D VLA models (left-bottom) achieve precise spatial perception through point clouds and voxels but sacrifice visual                                                   𝒵𝒵s

 interpretability. Our method bridges these paradigms by embedding spatial semantics into images via differentiable rendering.
                                  Abstract                                                                         calizing the next end-effector target with a world-aligned
                                                                                                                   cube marker, differentiably structuring surrounding geome-
 Robotic manipulation in complex 3D environments requires                                                          try whose color encodes spatial relations to the marker, and
 unifying spatial reasoning with intuitive visual perception,                                                      rendering adaptive viewpoints optimized to reveal the tar-
 which is a capability that current Vision-Language-Action                                                         get–environment spatial relationships. These differentiable
 paradigms address separately. While 3D VLAs excel in ge-                                                          images serve as visual bridges, embedding spatial seman-
 ometric and physical reasoning, they lack intuitive, image-                                                       tics while allowing gradients from 2D VLAs to backprop-
 level understanding and dense visual semantics; conversely,                                                       agate into 3D representations, thereby coupling geomet-
 2D VLAs (even with depth image) provide rich visual intu-                                                         ric reasoning with visual perception. This closed differen-
 ition and semantic continuity but miss explicit spatial global                                                    tiable loop unifies reasoning and perception, substantially
 grounding. We introduce DiffRender-VLA, a differentiable                                                          improving performance under occlusion, clutter, and com-
 rendering–based framework that bridges 3D and 2D Vision-                                                          plex spatial manipulation tasks, achieving average improve-
 Language-Action models through gradient-consistent vi-                                                            ments of +12.1% over state-of-the-art methods. Codes are
 sual mediation. It generates differentiable images by lo-                                                         available at https://github.com/zyl123456aB/DIFFVLA.
* Corresponding author is Xiu Su and Xiaoheng Deng

Robotic manipulation in complex 3D environments remains            gain under occlusion, 17.8% in cluttered scenes, and 13.4%
a central challenge in artificial intelligence and robotics.       in tasks requiring intricate spatial reasoning, consistently
Despite advances in computer vision [15], natural language         outperforming RGB- and RGB-D-based methods. These

    Recent research in vision-language-action (VLA) mod-              interpretable action policies.
els has advanced along two complementary directions. 3D            • We introduce a three-stage pipeline (localization, struc-
spatial VLAs, such as PerAct [39] and VoxPoser [17], em-              turing, and rendering) that transforms point-cloud geom-
phasize precise geometric reasoning through point clouds              etry into 2D representations embedding spatial semantics.

VLAs, such as RT-2 [4], OpenVLA [22], RoboMamba [2],                  gate into 3D representations.
and PaLM-E [9], leverage high-level semantics from im-             • We achieve state-of-the-art performance with +12.1%
ages but lack explicit 3D grounding. This dichotomy leaves            average improvement over existing methods, validated
a gap: 3D VLAs reason geometrically but fail to “see,”                across both simulation and real-world robotic systems.
while 2D VLAs perceive richly but fail to reason spatially.
